simple.meaning: צוֹק (tsôwq) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a strait , i.e. (figuratively) distress.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Proverbs 1:27. The surrounding context includes commandment.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צוֹק (H6695) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: צוֹק (tsôwq) / H6695 is traced through Proverbs 1:27, Isaiah 8:22, Isaiah 30:6, Daniel 9:25 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H6695. tsowq צוֺק noun [masculine] si vera lectio, constraint, distress ; — הָעִתִּים וּבְצוֺק Dan 9:25 usually in distressful times ; Gr וגו ׳וּבְקֵץ (so ᵐ5 [ 9:27 ] ᵑ6 ), as beginning of 9:26 , omitting וְ in וְאחרי (compare Bev Marti). צוּקָה noun feminine pressure, distress ; — national Isa 8:22 (+ צָרָה ), compare וְצ צָרָה ׳אֶרֶץ 30:6 ; personal וְצ ׳צָרָה Prov 1:27 .
